migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Ecosystem findings/citations were centrally re-adjudicated under the current runner-owned fixed rubric. Legacy language-local scores were not copied.

metric.installation_distribution_experie.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.artifact_integrity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Positive factor: the compiler is a dependency-free single-binary artifact with bundled libc/headers for cross-compilation, minimizing post-install friction once obtained, consistent with community guides describing Zig's minimalist toolchain philosophy.
component_findings.channel_breadth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Same rubric applies unchanged to all 10 languages. Five equally-weighted sub-criteria, each scored 0-100 then averaged: (1) official prebuilt binary coverage across major OS/arch with checksums/signatures and machine-readable index; (2) breadth/maturity of first-class OS package-manager integration (apt/dnf/brew/choco/winget as officially maintained or archive-included channels vs community-only/unstable); (3) availability and maturity of multi-version management tooling; (4) clarity/official-ness of documented install instructions; (5) first-run friction (dependency-free single artifact vs multi-step installer).
component_findings.install_docs: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Popularity/adoption of any given install channel was not used as a standalone proxy; findings rely on official docs, OS vendor docs, and package registry pages examined at a single fixed retrieval depth.
component_findings.installers: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): macOS has a de-facto easy path: <cite index="9-3">On macOS, brew install zig works well.</cite> but this is a community Homebrew formula, not a first-party channel.
component_findings.package_version_manager: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Manual install path is documented and simple: <cite index="5-1,5-2">Download a prebuilt version of Zig. Choose a build of Zig 0.15.2 for Linux that matches your CPU architecture.</cite> and after extraction <cite index="5-6">Consider getting Zig from a package manager such as chocolatey, scoop, or winget.</cite>

metric.installation_distribution_experie.limitations: Popularity/adoption of any given install channel was not used as a standalone proxy; findings rely on official docs, OS vendor docs, and package registry pages examined at a single fixed retrieval depth.
metric.installation_distribution_experie.selection_rule: Evaluate current official/de-facto installation paths on the same major desktop/server platforms and use only documented distribution channels.

metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.compat_deprecation: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Overall pattern: reproducible, signed, well-documented releases with disciplined patch tagging, but no inter-release compatibility guarantee and routine large-scale breaking changes each cycle, which the rubric's compatibility-guarantee and stability-commitment sub-criteria score low.
component_findings.governance_change: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Recent minor releases ship large breaking API changes as a matter of course: 0.15 reworked core stdlib types, e.g. <cite index="15-5,15-6">zig 0.15 replaced std.ArrayList with std.array_list.Managed as the default. the 'managed' variant now requires passing an allocator to every method call.</cite> and I/O redesign plus HTTP rework: <cite index="15-16">the change: zig 0.15 completely redesigned std.io.Reader and std.io.Writer interfaces.</cite> The 0.15.1 release notes themselves characterize this candidly: <cite index="11-13">the Writergate scandal, along with a slew of Language Changes and Standard Library cuts, rocks the boat with tidal waves of breaking API changes</cite>
component_findings.release_cadence: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Release cadence has historically been inconsistent: <cite index="18-6">the project's release schedule has been a bit inconsistent, with the release of version 0.14 being delayed several times</cite>, corroborated by the maintainer's own slipping estimate: <cite index="31-4,31-6">Previously, I made an estimate of January 1st for the 0.14.0 tag... That deadline slipped by mainly because I was caught up in a rather large branch</cite>
component_findings.release_integrity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Positive maturity signals: the project does issue dedicated bug-fix-only patch tags rather than folding fixes into the next feature release, e.g. <cite index="28-1,28-2">Bug fixes from 0.14.0 only. Please see the commits or issue tracker to learn which bugs have been fixed.</cite> for the 0.14.1 tag, and all release artifacts are cryptographically signed with a stable minisign key noted across multiple release pages.
component_findings.support_policy: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--zig): Release cadence has historically been inconsistent: <cite index="18-6">the project's release schedule has been a bit inconsistent, with the release of version 0.14 being delayed several times</cite>, corroborated by the maintainer's own slipping estimate: <cite index="31-4,31-6">Previously, I made an estimate of January 1st for the 0.14.0 tag... That deadline slipped by mainly because I was caught up in a rather large branch</cite>

metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.limitations: Elapsed time since first release and pre-1.0 status were noted only as contextual metadata and were not used as a scoring threshold or automatic penalty; the low score derives strictly from the absence of documented compatibility guarantees and the observed frequency/scope of breaking changes across the most recent release cycles.
metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.selection_rule: Score current observable release/support practices. Language age and first-release date are context only and never directly score.
